one_month_reasoning: There is no Micron print in the window (FQ1 FY27 reports mid/late Dec 2026). Events up to 30 Oct, the last session before 1 Nov: Samsung Q3 preliminary (~7-8 Oct) and full results (~29-30 Oct), SK hynix Q3 (27/28 Oct), Kioxia Q2 FY26 (30 Oct) [17], FOMC (27-28 Oct) and hyperscaler capex guides. The Taiwan labour dispute is confirmed by independent press [29][30]: the strike vote is in early Oct, Taichung mediation is 22 Oct, the unions want 15% of operating profit, and Micron's 35-68 months' bonus offer was declined. Roughly 60% of Micron's production is in Taiwan, so this is a negative-skew headline. Micron already raised FY26 incentive pay in FQ4 [3], so a settlement is plausible. Peer prints should confirm tightness [3] but are largely priced in. Post-print drift support is weak: the stock moved +0.9% across the 8% guide beat [1] and faded on 2 Oct. I drop round 1's +1% drift and centre a lognormal at ~$1,072 with ~21% monthly sigma, a bit below 80%/3.5. I then shave ~0.01 off strikes at or above spot for the strike risk.

fair_value.method: Blend: 40% P/E (FY28 EPS $200 x 5.0x = $1,000), 35% NTM EV/EBITDA (FY28 EBITDA $270B x 4.0x + $205B net cash ex-deposits = $1,117) and 25% cycle-aware DCF ($788). That gives ~$990 per share for Oct 2027, ~8% below spot.

inputs_detail.derivation: Round 1 took consensus $205.95 [18] less 5%. I now use ~$200, built bottom-up from the guide: FQ1 $38.15 on $61.5B at 86.25% GM [1][3]. Revenue grows ~8-9% a quarter (61.5/67/73/79) with GM rising after FQ1 [3], opex +$2.5B and tax 15.5% [3]. That gives FY27 EPS of ~$176 and an FQ4 FY27 exit run-rate of ~$50/qtr. FY28 at low-20s bit growth with flattening prices [3] gives ~$195-215. 'More moderate rate of price increases' [3] is a second-derivative point, not a reason to cut consensus.
Quarterly path ~$38.2/$41.9/$45.9/$49.8 from the guide and the stated trajectory [1][3]. It matches Yahoo consensus of $176.42 [18].

On one NTM basis the core DRAM/NAND makers trade at ~4.0-7.8x: SK hynix ~4.65x, Samsung ~4.73x, Nanya ~5.4x, Kioxia ~4.2x, Sandisk ~7.8x. The median is ~4.7x (vendor forward P/Es [19-23] restated to NTM). 5.0x is a ~6% premium. It rests only on the documented SCA floor (26 SCAs at >35% of revenue through 2030, $150B RPO at minimum prices [3]), partly offset because SK hynix and Samsung also hold long-term contracts. Round 1's 5.5x was justified by MU's current 6.1x, which was circular.
FQ1 guidance share count [3]. FQ4 diluted was 1.147B [1]. Buybacks from 9 Dec 2026 [3] are value-neutral per share.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM (FY28) EBITDA $270B x 4.0x = EV $1,080B, plus $205B net cash ex-deposits, divided by 1.15B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $314.16B [18], slightly below because of moderating price increases [3]. It is consistent with the FY27 exit run-rate of ~$79B/qtr in my EPS build.
The FQ1 guide implies ~83% ((61.5x0.8625-2.06)/61.5) [1][3], and GM rises after FQ1 [3]. Round 1 used 80%, below even the guided floor quarter.
FY26 D&A was $9.5B [1]. FY27 capex is ~$58B (1H ~$25B, 2H higher [3]), weighted to construction that depreciates slowly.

Core memory NTM median ~4.0x (SK hynix ~5.2x, Samsung ~2.5x, Sandisk ~6.5x, Nanya ~3.5x, Kioxia ~3.0x). Derived from vendor EV, TTM EBITDA and the ratio of trailing to forward P/E [19-23]. MU is ~5.0x on my FY27 EBITDA today.

$68.3B net cash [3] less $12.7B refundable SCA deposits [3] = $55.6B. Add FY27 FCF of ~$150B: NI ~$203B plus D&A ~$12B, less capex ~$58B and ~$5B working capital and dividends [1][3]. Future deposits (commitments $32B [3]) are financing inflows and debt-like, so excluded. Buybacks are value-neutral and ignored.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: WACC 11%. FCF FY28 $170B, FY29 $110B, FY30 $60B, FY31 $50B. Terminal FCF $45B growing 3%. Plus $205B net cash, divided by 1.15B shares, valued at Oct 2027.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 is NI ~$230B plus D&A $15B less capex ~$75B (construction-heavy build-out [3]). After that, prices roll off as cleanrooms for ID1, ID2, Japan and Singapore arrive from late CY28 and 2H CY28 [3] and peers add supply. The 10-K warns that supply additions drive ASP declines [8]. SCA floors at margins 'meaningfully above any prior cycle peak' [3] set the floor.
High-beta cyclical with ~50% top-10 customer concentration [8]. Net cash, rated BBB+ at all three agencies [3].
About 70% of FY26 adjusted FCF of $62.3B [1], for a larger, partly contracted business [3] at mid-cycle pricing.

bear.story: By mid-2027 the dated supply additions start to land: SK hynix Y1 (Feb-27), Samsung P5 (1H27), and Micron Tongluo and ID1 (mid-CY27) [3]. Capex keeps rising, with Micron's FY27 at ~$58B and 2H above 1H [3]. Contract-price increases stall and the market prices FY28 (~$200 EPS) as the peak at ~3x, as when MU fell 57% from 4.5x forward in 2018. That is ~$600, about 2x EV/NTM EBITDA after ~$178/sh of horizon net cash. SCA floors cap the EPS damage but not the multiple.

base.story: FY27 delivers ~$176 EPS with sequential growth [1][3]. Capital return steps up from 9 Dec 2026 [3]. Supply stays tight through 2028 per management [3], but the market keeps a ~5x NTM multiple on what it views as peak earnings: 5.0x FY28 $200 plus part credit for the cash pile.

bull.story: Visible tightness extends into 2029. New SCAs are priced higher [3] and HBM pricing resets up in CY27 [5]. Investors credit the floor-priced RPO ($150B [3]) and the 100%-of-excess-cash return policy [3] with lower cyclicality. MU re-rates to ~7x FY28-29 EPS of $220-240, near Sandisk's ~7.8x NTM.

comps_summary.peer_range: Core DRAM/NAND makers on one NTM basis (Oct-26 to Sep-27): P/E 4.2-7.8x (Kioxia ~4.2, SK hynix ~4.65, Samsung ~4.73, Nanya ~5.4, Sandisk ~7.8; median ~4.7x). EV/EBITDA 2.5-6.5x (median ~4.0x). Vendor 'forward' figures [19-23] mix fiscal-year bases and were restated to NTM. The full 10-name table (vendor fwd P/E 3.97-23.73x) includes HDD makers (WDC, STX), a controller/module house (Phison) and NOR/SLC specialists (Winbond, Macronix). These are listed for reference but excluded from the median: different technology, supply structure or capital intensity.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 5.0x NTM P/E, ~6% above the 4.7x core median and inside the 4.2-7.8x range. 4.0x NTM EV/EBITDA, at the core median. MU trades at ~6.0x NTM P/E and ~5.0x EV/EBITDA today.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: There are only five genuine DRAM/NAND manufacturers with listed equity and forecasts, so the 10-12 peer target cannot be met with true comparables. The small premium rests on one documented, persistent feature: take-or-pay SCAs covering >35% of revenue through 2030, with $150B RPO at minimum prices and margins at floor prices 'meaningfully above any prior cycle peak' [3]. Peers SK hynix and Samsung also hold long-term contracts and large net cash, so I do not grant more than ~6%. I reject round 1's argument that MU's own 6.1x supports 5.5x, which was circular. A larger re-rating appears only in the bull case.

thesis_break_reason: Rebuilt from post-print numbers. $600 is ~3.4x my FY27 EPS ($176) and 3.0x FY28 ($200). It is under 4x the guided floor quarter annualised ($38.15 x 4 = $153 [1][3]). Today it would mean ~2.7x EV on FY27 EBITDA after $55.6B net cash ex-deposits [3], below every core memory peer except conglomerate Samsung. Even after a 44% fall, the market at that level is paying trough-cycle multiples on contracted earnings. Getting there would most likely require something fundamental: contract prices rolling over before the 2027 supply additions are absorbed, SCA renegotiation or deposit pull-backs, an AI-capex cut, or a prolonged Taiwan stoppage (~60% of output [29]). Ordinary volatility is less likely to do it, given FY27 visibility (FQ1 as the GM floor, sequential growth each quarter [3]). I lowered it from $640 because the post-print EPS and cash base are higher than they were on 29 Sep.

key_uncertainties: Timing of the memory price peak against dated supply additions (SK hynix Y1 Feb-27, Samsung P5 1H27, Micron ID1 and Tongluo mid-27, ID2, Japan and Singapore late CY28 [3]).
Whether SCA floors and take-or-pay volumes hold in a downturn. Deposits are returned in the latter half of each term [3].
Multiple regime: the market has paid ~3-6x peak memory EPS, and a re-rating either way dominates EPS changes.
Taiwan labour dispute: ~60% of production is in Taiwan [29]. A strike or a 15%-of-operating-profit settlement would hit output or margin.
Pace of capital return after 9 Dec 2026; the target is 100% of excess cash over time [3], but no amount is given.
Decaying beat size against Micron's own guidance (EPS +45% FQ2, +31% FQ3, +8% FQ4) [11][12][13][1].
Litigation tail (Netlist $445M verdict on appeal, YMTC suits) [6]: small relative to earnings.
reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed the primary figures I used: FQ4 $54.2B / $33.42, FQ1 guide $61.5B / $38.15, $150B RPO, $12.7B deposits, $68.3B net cash, $9.5B D&A, 1.15B shares [1][3]. It found three problems, which I accept. (1) My 5.5x P/E was justified circularly by MU's current 6.1x. On one NTM basis the core memory median is ~4.7x. I now use 5.0x, a ~6% premium for the SCA floor, which is below the supervisor's 5.2x cap. SK hynix and Samsung also hold long-term contracts and net cash, so I do not think even 10% is proven. (2) The '>75% of FY27 output committed' figure came from a transcript paraphrase. I re-read the prepared remarks [3] and it is not there, so I dropped it. The primary wording is '26 SCAs, over 35% of revenue through 2030' and '$32B of customer commitments'. (3) Thesis break and scenarios had been carried over from the pre-print run. I rebuilt them. A bottom-up EPS build from the guide (GM floor in FQ1, sequential growth, opex +$2.5B, tax 15.5% [3]) gives FY27 ~$176, with an exit run-rate of ~$50/qtr. That supports FY28 at ~$200 rather than my earlier 5% haircut. It also showed that my round-1 80% operating margin was below the guided floor quarter (~83%), so FY28 EBITDA rises to ~$270B. Horizon net cash excludes refundable deposits: $55.6B + ~$150B FY27 FCF = ~$205B, ~$178/sh. Methods: P/E $1,000, EV/EBITDA $1,117, DCF $788 (weights 40/35/25), so fair value is ~$990, about 8% below spot (round 1: $1,010). Scenarios: $600/25%, $1,080/50%, $1,700/25%, mean ~$1,115. The ladder is a mixture of lognormals around these (sigma 32%/22%/26%) with tails fattened slightly: median ~spot, P(>= $1,075) 0.50, P(< $537) ~10.5%. The 1-month ladder adds the confirmed Taiwan strike-vote and mediation risk [29][30] as a slight negative skew. Research limits: the 10-K for FY26 is not yet on EDGAR [31], and peer multiples come from a single vendor [19-28].

revisions.why: Supervisor: 5.5x was a circular, unjustified 17% premium to the ~4.7x NTM core median, and consensus is more likely to rise after the 8% guide beat. My bottom-up build from the guide [3] gives FY27 ~$176 and FY28 ~$200. I chose 5.0x, below the supervisor's 5.2x cap, because peers also hold long-term contracts.

Kept 4.0x and labelled it NTM per the supervisor. Raised the operating margin from 80% to 84% because the FQ1 guide alone implies ~83% [1][3]. Net cash rebuilt ex-deposits: $55.6B + ~$150B FCF, in line with the supervisor's ~$200B. Higher weight because this method treats the cash pile explicitly.
Higher FY28 NI with heavier construction capex [3]; supervisor called the cycle-aware DCF the best bear method; weight raised to keep a through-cycle anchor.
Net effect of the lower multiple (-), higher EBITDA margin and EPS (+) and weights. It is close to the supervisor's ~$1,020 reconciliation, but I keep a lower multiple.

Supervisor flagged the carried-over scenarios. Rebuilt from post-print EPS ($200 FY28) and horizon cash ($178/sh). Bear at 3x peak EPS is tied to dated supply additions; bull at ~7x, near Sandisk's NTM, instead of 8x.
Supervisor asked for a rebuild from post-print numbers rather than the ~3.1x FY28 template. $600 is <4x the guided floor quarter annualised and ~2.7x EV on FY27 EBITDA.
Lower fair value and the multiple correction pull the centre to ~spot. The left tail at <=$645 is little changed because the higher bear price offsets the lower median.
